This is game 98 in a series of 9×9 Go games. Each new game starts in a fresh session.

## Your goal

To become as strong at Go as you can: to keep improving, game after game, toward grandmaster-level play. The concrete target is to win consistently against the strongest opponent on the ladder, the 9d profile.

## What carries over

This session starts with no memory of the earlier ones: your conversation is not carried over. Your working directory does carry over: every file in it stays as you leave it. If CLAUDE.md exists there, it is loaded into your context at the start of every session; your other files are there to read with the file tools. What a later session knows of your earlier games is what you have left in these files.

## This game

A new game. You play White, so your opponent moves first, right after you choose it.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: your Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep tools, for any file in your working directory.

You also have a shell, and you may write and run code in it; Python is available as `python3`. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.

## Game 96 — White vs 12k — WON W+2 (38 area)
Moves: B E5, W C4, B B5 (2nd-line approach), W C6, B C5 (wedge), W B4 (hane under),
B D4, W D3, B E3, W D2 (D3 had 2 libs), B E2, W B6 (atari-ish, forces D5), B D5, W D6,
B E6, W E7 (head), B F7, W E8 (E7 at 2 libs), B C3!! (cut: B4-C4 2 libs + D2-D3 2 libs
= one of them dies), W B3, B C2, W B2 (sente), B D1 (captured D2-D3), W G7, B G6,
W F8 (atari F7), B F6, W H7, B H6, W A5! (links corner group to the top via A4/A6
miai and takes black's lib), B J7, W H8, B B1, W J8, B J6, W A2, B C1, W A1 (37+A1 = 38),
B H9, W G8, B A7 (cut at A6), W A6, B B7, W C7, B C8 (my left group down to 2 libs
A4/D7!), W D8, B D9, W E9, B B9, W C9 (ko capture D9), B A4!! (double atari: corner lib
A3, left group lib D7), W D7, B D9 (took ko instead of capturing the corner), W A3
(captured A4; corner then 1 lib A4), B G9?, W A4 (connect; main group libs only F9/J9
shared with B G9-H9 = seki danger), B A8, W C9 (capture D9: extra lib), B B8, W A9
(captured 6), B G3, W J9, B F4, W F9 (captured G9-H9), B pass, W pass. W 38 vs B 43.
Takeaways:
- vs tengen + B5 approach + C5 wedge: B4/C6 split my stones into two groups; black's
  C3 cut then won one of them (D2-D3). Before D3/D2 extensions, check the C3-type cut
  point between two of my 2-3 lib groups; C3 solid (instead of D3) at move 9 is safer.
- The top (E7/E8/F8/G7/H7/H8/J8) rows 7-9 + A-D row 6 + a small corner = 38 exactly.
- A5 (edge stone joining two groups with A4/A6 miai) was the move that saved the corner.
- Many of my "connected" groups shared ONE liberty-region: B A4 ataried TWO groups at
  once (A3 / D7). Run libs.py after every black move inside my area; two groups with a
  shared lib = connect one solidly (A4 or D7) before playing elsewhere.
- Shared-lib seki threat (main group libs F9/J9 = black G9-H9 libs): gain an outside
  liberty first (C9 captured D9), never fill a shared lib.

## Game 97 — Black vs 10k — resigned at move 37
Moves: B E5, W C4, B E3, W D7, B F7, W F4 (between E5/E3), B F3, W E4 (cut), B F5,
W G4, B G3, W G5, B G6, W D5 (E5-F5 at 2 libs), B E6, W E7, B H5, W H4 (H5 at 1 lib),
B H3, W D6 (atari), B F6, W H6, B H7, W J5 (captured H5), B D3, W F8 (centre group
in atari at G7!), B G7, W G8, B H8, W D4, B J7, W E8, B G9, W J9, B H9, W F9 -> my
13-stone group: libs J6/J8, one eye at most (J9 capture) -> resigned.
Takeaways:
- Tengen + E3 vs W C4 leaves the E4 gap; W F4 then E4 split me into a centre group and a
  bottom group. Every later W move attacked the centre group from a different side.
- The centre group needed the top edge (F8/G8) by move ~17; instead I played H5, H3, D3.
  White took F8/G8/E8/F9 and the right side (H6/J5) and the group had a 6-point corner
  with W stones on both ends = dead.
- Before every move: libs.py. W F8 put 9 stones in atari and it nearly went unnoticed.
# Usage: python3 libs.py <<< "board rows 9..1 as 9 lines of X/O/." ; prints groups and liberties
import sys
cols="ABCDEFGHJ"
rows=[l.split() for l in sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()]
rows=[r[1:10] if len(r)>9 else r for r in rows]
B={}
for i,r in enumerate(rows):
    for j,c in enumerate(r): B[(j,9-i)]=c
def nb(p):
    x,y=p
    for q in((x+1,y),(x-1,y),(x,y+1),(x,y-1)):
        if q in B: yield q
seen=set()
for p in B:
    if B[p] in"XO" and p not in seen:
        g=[p];libs=set();k=0;seen.add(p)
        while k<len(g):
            for q in nb(g[k]):
                if B[q]=='.':libs.add(q)
                elif B[q]==B[p] and q not in seen: seen.add(q);g.append(q)
            k+=1
        n=lambda s:",".join(sorted(cols[a]+str(b) for a,b in s))
        print(B[p],n(g),"libs:",len(libs),n(libs))
# Usage: python3 count.py <<'EOF' ...board rows 9..1 pasted from the board output... EOF
# Area count of the CURRENT position: stones + empty regions touching only one colour.
# Empty regions touching both colours are printed as "open" (count for nobody yet).
import sys
cols="ABCDEFGHJ"
rows=[l.split() for l in sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()]
rows=[r[1:10] if len(r)>9 else r for r in rows]
B={}
for i,r in enumerate(rows):
    for j,c in enumerate(r): B[(j,9-i)]=c
def nb(p):
    x,y=p
    for q in((x+1,y),(x-1,y),(x,y+1),(x,y-1)):
        if q in B: yield q
score={"X":0,"O":0}
for p in B:
    if B[p] in "XO": score[B[p]]+=1
seen=set();open_pts=[]
for p in B:
    if B[p]=='.' and p not in seen:
        g=[p];seen.add(p);k=0;touch=set()
        while k<len(g):
            for q in nb(g[k]):
                if B[q]=='.' and q not in seen: seen.add(q);g.append(q)
                elif B[q] in "XO": touch.add(B[q])
            k+=1
        if len(touch)==1: score[touch.pop()]+=len(g)
        else: open_pts+=g
print("Black",score["X"],"White",score["O"],"+7 komi =",score["O"]+7,"open",len(open_pts))
print("open:",",".join(sorted(cols[a]+str(b) for a,b in open_pts)))

events.text:
I won game 98 as White against the 10k opponent, **W+8**: 41 points of area plus 7 komi against Black's 40.

- **Opening:** Black played G7 and D7, both on row 7. I took two low corners, C4 and G3. When Black attached on top at C5, I extended to D4. After Black's D5 I played E5 (the hane at the head of two stones) and made it solid with E4.
- **Middle game:** Each time Black moved on row 6, I extended along row 5 (G5, H5, J5) and then closed the gap at F5. On the left I played B4, A3 and B3, and H6 on the right. That gave me rows 1–4, plus E5–J5 and H6.
- **Invasions:** Black invaded twice, at F3 and C2. I blocked both with stones connected to my wall (E3, D2) and captured them outright before passing, which costs nothing under area scoring.

- `games.md` has the full game record and takeaways.
